transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-03-03 15:00 UTC | Duration: 45m | Attendees: Sofia Martinez, Daniel Kim (Redwood); Priya Shah, Liam O'Connor, Maya Patel (HarborTrust)

[00:00] Sofia (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick check-in, we'll go 45 minutes. Daniel and I will cover the security asks from last week and see where you are on audit log schema.
[00:15] Priya (HarborTrust): Yeah thanks. We had a quick internal follow up, still aligning on retention windows. We've got legal wanting 7 years for certain PII, but ops prefer 1 year for perf. So we need to know what options Redwood supports.
[00:28] Daniel (Redwood SE): Right, we support configurable retention per tenant, we can do short-term cache for KV and longer-term audit logs. To be clear, there are two layers: per-request telemetry stored in the service with 30/90/365 day tiers and then the audit export to your SIEM which you control retention for.
[00:45] Liam (HarborTrust): When you say audit export, is that push to S3 or pull via API? We're under a strict egress control.
[00:52] Daniel: We can do both. For the Private deployment we can set up cross-account S3 with SSE-KMS, or we can stream logs via a secure forwarder to your Splunk/ELK. We also have an option to keep logs in the customer's VPC only.
[01:10] Priya: Important for us is the field-level detail. We need request metadata, prompt hash, model id, model version, response length, and a redacted prompt option. Can you capture prompt hash not full prompt?
[01:22] Daniel: Yes, prompt hashing is supported. We can store only hashes for PII-sensitive pipelines and keep a redact toggle. Full transcript storage is an opt-in. The audit schema is flexible; I'll send the example schema after the call.
[01:35] Maya (Compliance): Also wondering about SSO: we plan to use our Okta instance, SAML 2.0. How does Redwood handle SCIM for provisioning and group-based RBAC?
[01:45] Sofia: We support SAML for SSO and SCIM for user sync; RBAC maps groups from IdP to roles in the Console. There can be a mismatch sometimes in group names so we recommend a small mapping table.
[02:00] Priya: Are sessions logged for admin actions? We need admin audit trail.
[02:05] Daniel: Yep, admin actions (policy changes, key rotations, role assignments) are in audit logs with actor, timestamp, IP. We also include session context when available.
[02:18] Liam: Network question - for private deployment will we need peering? Our security team prefers VPC peering with no public endpoints.
[02:28] Daniel: For Private we can provision in your VPC or set up a peered VPC in our cloud region. There's also an on-prem appliance option if you need air-gapped. We'll share network diagrams but we need your internal IP ranges and any firewall restrictions.
[02:45] Priya: KMS - do you support BYOK with HSM-backed keys? We need to ensure keys never leave our control.
[02:55] Daniel: Yes, we support customer-managed keys (AWS KMS, GCP KMS) and can integrate with HSM-backed services. For truly sealed keys we offer envelope encryption so plaintext model payloads aren't accessible in Redwood control plane.
[03:12] Maya: SOC 2 - can you provide Type II report and recent pen test?
[03:18] Sofia: Absolutely. We have SOC 2 Type II, annual pen-test summaries, and third-party assessments. I'll attach the artifacts.
[03:25] Priya: Great. Also need clarification on who can access the cached KV - is the cache stored per-tenant?
[03:32] Daniel: Cache is namespace-scoped per customer by default. For Dedicated/Private it's isolated to your pool. There was a note last week about cross-tenant leakage - we don't allow that in Dedicated or Private.
[03:44] Liam: On performance, we're going to run a small benchmark for throughput at 500 concurrent requests. Will the Dedicated pool support horizontal autoscaling?
[03:54] Daniel: Yes, Dedicated pools can autoscale within configured bounds. We can also provide a burst capacity policy. For the pilot we'll run a 1k token average test and share latency distribution.
[04:10] Priya: One outstanding legal ask: can you provide an auditable trail of all data exports? We need to show a list of sinks and who initiated exports.
[04:20] Sofia: We have export audit events that include the actor and destination. We can also produce periodic export reports for compliance.
[04:30] Maya: On PII redaction - if we choose to redact prompts, how do we validate model quality doesn't degrade?
[04:40] Daniel: Good question. We recommend using a hashed-plus-redaction mode and run parallel A/B tests during pilot. Redwood Optimize can track quality regressions against baseline evals and flag if the redaction pipeline causes drift.
[04:55] Priya: Anything else on SOC/controls?
[05:00] Sofia: We'll send the SOC 2 Type II, pen-test summary, network diagram, and a sample audit schema. Also pricing addendum for Dedicated pilot.
[05:10] Priya: Sounds good. We'll send audit field list and our IP ranges by end of week.
[05:18] Sofia: Ok next steps recap... (brief recap) Daniel will run the dedicated benchmark and share results, I will send SOC2 and pricing. Schedule on-site review for week of the 9th.
[05:35] Liam: Quick note, competitor comparison - we looked at OpenAI private endpoints and Anthropic, but our ops team worried about vendor lock and egress costs.
[05:45] Sofia: Understood. We try to keep the deployment consistent so you can move between Hosted and Dedicated with minimal changes.
[05:55] Priya: Thanks everyone.
[06:00] End of recording.
